ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$, $DE\perp AB$, intersecting $AC$ at $E$. If $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{5}{3}$, then what is the value of $\tan\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BE. Since $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $DE \perp AB$, it follows that AE = BE. Since $\frac{AE}{EC} = \frac{5}{3}$, we can set AE = BE = 5k and CE = 3k. By the Pythagorean theorem, we get BC = 4k. Therefore, AC = AE + CE = 8k. Therefore, $\tan A = \frac{BC}{AC} = \frac{4k}{8k} = \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$.

method.method_draft: First read the figure as a right triangle ABC with A on the left, B on the lower right, C above B, E lying on segment AC, and D lying on segment AB with segment DE drawn from D to E. From the text, use that angle ACB is 90 degrees, D is the midpoint of AB, DE is perpendicular to AB, and AE:EC = 5:3. Since D is the midpoint of AB and DE is perpendicular to AB, line DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, so any point on DE is equidistant from A and B; hence AE = BE. Set AE = BE = 5k and EC = 3k, so AC = 8k. In right triangle BEC, the hypotenuse is BE = 5k and one leg is EC = 3k, so by the Pythagorean theorem BC = 4k. Finally, in right triangle ABC, tan angle A = opposite/adjacent = BC/AC = 4k/8k = 1/2.

From AE:EC = 5:3, let AE = 5k and EC = 3k, then BE = AE = 5k, AC = AE + EC = 8k. In right triangle BEC, BE is the hypotenuse, EC = 3k, BE = 5k, so by the Pythagorean theorem, BC = 4k. Finally, in right triangle ABC, tan∠A = opposite side/adjacent side = BC/AC = 4k/8k = 1/2.
